title: Machine learning for risk profiling: An analysis of pension fund participants
authors: Goncu, A.; Kuzubas, T. U.; Saltoglu, B.
tldr: Compares ML models to regulatory benchmark for profiling risk of 81,563 Turkish pension fund participants, finding boosting methods yield modest improvements and 4 variables match full questionnaire performance.
problem_and_motivation: Risk profiling in pension systems relies on lengthy questionnaires causing participant friction and low completion rates. ML may identify informative variables and capture nonlinear relationships missed by regulatory scoring.
approach: Analyzed 81,563 participants from a major Turkish pension fund company (2018-2022).
Compared various ML models (boosting, random forest, SVM, etc.) to the regulatory CMB risk score.
Used Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) to identify most informative predictors.
Evaluated models on predicting actual portfolio risk (continuous measure from fund allocations).
Tested 4-variable reduced model against full questionnaire models.
findings: num: Boosting methods yield modest improvements in predictive accuracy relative to regulatory risk score.
num: All models show modest explanatory power (R-squared 0.13-0.17).
num: Performance using just 4 variables is comparable to using full questionnaire.
Self-reported risk attitude and age (nonlinear relationship) are most important predictors.
Age shows inverted-U relationship with risk-taking, peaking at 35-44 age group.
ML can enhance risk profiling by identifying informative variables and capturing nonlinearities.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Demonstrates ML can enhance regulatory risk profiling by identifying key predictive variables and capturing nonlinear age effects. Shows 4-variable model matches full questionnaire performance, enabling simplified onboarding. Provides empirical evidence that boosting methods modestly outperform regulatory risk scores.
directly_justifies: Boosting methods modestly improve accuracy over regulatory risk score.
Four variables match performance of full risk questionnaire.
Self-reported risk attitude and age are strongest predictors.
Age shows inverted-U relationship with portfolio risk.
limits: R-squared remains modest (0.13-0.17) across all models.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematically scanned all domains. Assigned 5.B, 5.C, 6.A, 12.B high relevance. Assigned 7.E medium for onboarding. Rejected mobile UX and security topics as paper focuses on ML profiling.

limitations: Modest explanatory power (R-squared 0.13-0.17) across all models.
Single Turkish pension company data may not generalize to other markets.
Cross-sectional design limits causal inference about risk preferences.
